message.content:
The title “best jazz singer” is highly subjective and depends on what you value—vocal technique, emotional depth, influence, or innovation. However, a few names consistently appear at the top of most lists:

| Singer | Why they’re often considered the best |
|--------|---------------------------------------|
| **Ella Fitzgerald** | Known as the “First Lady of Song,” her impeccable pitch, scat‑sing mastery, and flawless phrasing set a gold standard for jazz vocalists. |
| **Billie Holiday** | Her unique phrasing, emotional intensity, and ability to convey deep feeling made her a pioneer in jazz interpretation. |
| **Louis Armstrong** (trumpet & voice) | Though primarily a trumpeter, his gravelly, charismatic singing style helped popularize jazz worldwide. |
| **Frank Sinatra** | A master of phrasing and timing, he blended jazz with pop sensibilities, influencing generations of singers. |
| **Nat King Cole** | His smooth baritone and lyrical delivery bridged jazz and early R&B, leaving a lasting legacy. |

If you’re looking for a single “best” singer, many would argue **Ella Fitzgerald** due to her technical brilliance and lasting influence. But the beauty of jazz is that it thrives on diversity, so each of these artists brings something uniquely valuable to the genre.
